name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Thursday 27 February 1975

solutions.check: 29 entries, 58 crossings, 0 conflicts, agrees with the 1 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Town backed Saxon king, in two ways

indicators.note: something backed goes into reverse, so the king's name is read from its end
the king sits in the middle of the other material, held inside it

blocks.note: two abbreviations for roads: ST for street and RD for road
Offa was the eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for his dyke

explanation.surface: A town is said to have supported an old Saxon king, perhaps in two different senses.
explanation.walkthrough: "In two ways" looks like a comment on the town's loyalty, but the ways are two roads, ST and RD, that hold the reversed OFFA: ST + AFFO + RD = STAFFORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Ground rent IRA collected

indicators.note: letters that are collected are gathered up and put together anew, in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paramilitaries gather in the rent due on a piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ground rent" reads as a single legal phrase, but "Ground" is the definition and "rent" is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, a synonym for ground.

clue.text: Try to catch railwaymen in port

blocks.note: to fish for something is to try to catch it
a guard is the railwayman who rides at the back of a train

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to arrest striking rail workers down at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: Fishguard is a ferry port in Pembrokeshire, Wales, sailing to Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishguard is a Welsh harbour town with ferry crossings to Rosslare, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Playwright's singular misfortune

blocks.note: singular means just one
an ill is a misfortune or trouble

explanation.surface: A dramatist suffers a strange, unusual piece of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: "Singular" pretends to mean odd, describing the misfortune; here it means one in number.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was the American dramatist who wrote Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: CID receives most eccentric types for such employment

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and irregular, so these letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The detectives' department takes on some very odd characters.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force; the three words supply all fifteen letters, and the closing phrase points at the kind of job the shuffled result names.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic service is working as a household servant, the employment of maids, cooks and butlers.

clue.text: Unpretentious . fashion centre of Boston

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the two letters at its heart are kept

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion or style
the two middle letters of the six-letter city

explanation.surface: Down-to-earth clothes are what's in style in the middle of Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray dot in the clue is a printing blemish in the scanned newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone modest makes no show of themselves, which is what unpretentious describes.

clue.text: Bureaucrat makes speech in Pekin

blocks.note: first meaning: a senior and powerful civil servant
second meaning: the standard Chinese language spoken in Peking (Beijing)

explanation.surface: A government official delivers an address in the Chinese capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Pekin is an old spelling of Peking, now Beijing. The original mandarins were officials of imperial China, which is how the word came to mean a senior civil servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a top civil servant and the official Chinese language of the capital.

clue.text: No-one aggrieved and upset — all eating away!.

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, and all says the whole string is flipped

blocks.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
someone sore is aggrieved or resentful

explanation.surface: Nobody is resentful or upset, while everyone sits down to a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: "No-one" looks like a single word meaning nobody, but it splits in two. In a down clue the whole chain is written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of rock or soil by water and wind, so eating away is a fair gloss.

clue.text: Management tried to remedy cases of ill-feeling?

definitions.text: tried to remedy cases of ill-feeling

blocks.note: first meaning: the way something is handled or dealt with

blocks.clueFragment: tried to remedy cases of ill-feeling
blocks.note: second meaning: medical care given to cure the sick

explanation.surface: Bosses attempt to settle grievances among unhappy staff.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ill-feeling" suggests resentment in an office; read literally it is feeling ill, and the care given for it is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment means both how something is handled and the medical care a doctor gives to patients.

clue.text: Fish swears to reform

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again in a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows to mend their ways, perhaps a fisherman giving up cursing.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish of rocky coasts, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Tree supplies someone with a little wood

blocks.note: a man is a person, someone
a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: A tree provides a person with some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: "A little wood" seems to mean some timber from the tree; it is a small group of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangrove is a tropical tree that grows in coastal swamps on stilt-like roots.

clue.text: Fruit's about £500 — and cattle-food

indicators.note: about means around, so the fruit word wraps itself around the money

blocks.note: mangos is a plural of mango, a tropical fruit
L is the abbreviation for the pound sign, from Latin libra
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Fruit is said to be costing about five hundred pounds, along with animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: "£500" reads as a price, but splits into two letters, L and D, which go inside MANGOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangolds, or mangel-wurzels, are large beets grown as winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Drug taker perhaps did wrong to break the law

indicators.note: something done wrong is muddled, so these letters are put in the wrong order
to break into something is to burst inside it, so these letters go into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: an Act of Parliament is a law
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug user commits the crime of breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: "Did wrong" reads as committed an offence; it is DID scrambled to DDI, which breaks into ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is someone dependent on a habit; a drug taker is one example, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Biblical priest given change once in India

blocks.note: first meaning: the high priest before whom Jesus was brought after his arrest
second meaning: small coins formerly used in India, sixteen to the rupee

explanation.surface: A priest from the scriptures is handed some loose coins on a trip to India long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: "Change" looks like a transformation but means coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Annas is the high priest named in John's Gospel, and annas were the copper coins of colonial India.

clue.text: Plants need sea air, Tim recollected

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means gathered up again in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener named Tim remembered that his plants need a breath of coastal air.
explanation.walkthrough: "Recollected" pretends to mean remembered; split as re-collected, it says gather the letters again.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic herbs and shrubs including wormwood, sagebrush and tarragon.

clue.text: Continental transport industry?

blocks.note: first meaning: a public stagecoach once used in France and elsewhere in Europe
second meaning: hard-working effort and application

explanation.surface: The clue poses as a question about the European haulage business.
explanation.walkthrough: "Industry" reads as a business sector; it means hard work. Continental is the British word for mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence is both careful hard work and the old French stagecoach, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Poor Green gets call-up, being 25, perhaps

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so the colour word's letters are spoiled into a new order
in a down clue up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
to cite someone is to call or summon them to appear in court

explanation.surface: A hard-up man named Green receives his conscription papers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Call-up" looks like military conscription; it splits into call and up. The definition refers to 25-across, ACTIVE, which the answer exemplifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone energetic is lively and vigorous, a fair example of being active.

clue.text: Game attempt to get a photograph

blocks.note: snap is a card game in which players call out on matching cards
a shot is an attempt, as in have a shot

explanation.surface: Playing a game, someone tries to take a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly, so it is a kind of photograph.

clue.text: Unpunctuality of badly trained Nazi bodyguard

indicators.note: badly done means botched, so the letters of the word it describes are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the SS, the Schutzstaffel, began as Hitler's personal bodyguard

explanation.surface: Poorly drilled guards turn up late, a failing of a sloppy unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness, the failure to arrive on time, which is what unpunctuality means.

clue.text: Army suppliers also lost nothing to these rogues

indicators.note: nothing is the round letter for zero, and lost says that letter drops out of the word before it

blocks.note: the Royal Army Service Corps, which supplied the British Army
taken as written

explanation.surface: Army quartermasters lost nothing to a gang of thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: "Lost nothing" sounds like a reassurance; it tells you to drop O (nothing) from ALSO, leaving ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascals are mischievous or dishonest people, close synonyms of rogues.

clue.text: Distance covered in a river steamer

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped up inside, so the answer lies concealed within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of river and the start of steamer

explanation.surface: A paddle boat travels a long way along a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A verst is an old Russian unit of length, a little over a kilometre.

clue.text: Woman hails signs of harvest?

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
ave is the Latin greeting hail, so aves are hails

explanation.surface: A woman greets the first signs that the crops are ripening.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hails" could be a hailstorm spoiling a harvest; it is the Latin greeting ave.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaves are bundles of cut corn stood up in the field, a familiar sight at harvest time.

clue.text: Notes the month the girl turned up-

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means flipped to read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Oct is the calendar abbreviation for October
Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A note records the month in which a young woman arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: "Notes" looks like a written memo; it is musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is the run of eight notes from one pitch to the same pitch an interval higher.

clue.text: Accident by motorway — fell

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's first long motorway, with the 1 written as I
Shap Fell is a high moorland pass in Cumbria on the road to Scotland

explanation.surface: A crash beside the motorway, after which someone fell.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fell" pretends to be the past tense of fall; it is a northern English word for a hill, here Shap Fell, notorious for winter road closures.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, usually a minor one.

clue.text: Could be one of our betters of course!

definitions.text: Could be one of our betters of course!

blocks.note: surface reading: one of our social superiors, the people above us
setter's reading: people who place bets, found at a racecourse

explanation.walkthrough: "Betters" means superiors, but also people who bet; "of course" sounds like naturally, but means at the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends horse races typically places wagers there, so a punter at the track fits.

clue.text: Take man for a sailor in port?

blocks.note: first meaning: to kidnap a man and force him to serve as a sailor
second meaning: China's great seaport

explanation.surface: Someone mistakes a man in a harbour for a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: "Take man for a sailor" reads as mistaking someone's identity; it means abducting him for a crew. Sailors were so often pressed for voyages to China that the city lent its name to the practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is both the Chinese port city and a verb for forcing a man into service at sea.

clue.text: Brisk sort of voice

blocks.note: first meaning: lively and energetic
second meaning: the grammatical voice in which the subject performs the action

explanation.walkthrough: "Voice" suggests singing or speaking; it is the grammar term, as in active versus passive voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Active means busy and energetic, and is also the grammatical voice contrasted with the passive.

clue.text: We are ' more fond of . such friends?

blocks.note: surface reading: a statement that we like certain friends better than others
setter's reading: the proverb that the heart grows fonder of those who are away

explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the saying that absence makes the heart grow fonder, and on the toast to friends who are not present. The stray marks are printing blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends who are away are the ones the proverb says we grow fonder of, the subject of a traditional toast.

clue.text: Perhaps doctor's prescription is cut out without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the surgery word stands around the pause

blocks.note: to excise is to cut out, as a surgeon does
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription is cut short without any dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: "Without hesitation" reads as promptly; here "without" has its old sense of outside, so the pause sits inside the surgical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors often recommend physical activity to patients, so exercise is one example of what they prescribe.
